sub: Named after the “groups” (zumar) driven to Hell and Paradise in ayat 71 and 73
theme: Worship Allah alone, sincerely (ikhlāṣ), with nothing mixed in. The surah repeats this from every angle: proofs of tawḥīd, the emptiness of shirk, and a call to return to Allah’s mercy before the Day.
story: Revealed in Makkah, reportedly before the emigration to Abyssinia, at a time of persecution. Ayah 10, “Allah’s earth is spacious,” is linked to Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib and his companions deciding to emigrate there.

It is a sermon aimed mainly at the disbelieving Quraysh, with the believers addressed here and there. Its one message: serve Allah sincerely and mix nothing into that worship. Tawḥīd and its fruits, shirk and its ruin, are shown again and again.

Believers are told: if a place becomes too narrow for worship, emigrate. The Prophet ﷺ is told to say plainly that persecution will not move him. Some reports call a few ayat Madinan, especially 53. The Prophet ﷺ reportedly recited this surah every night.

sections.title: Sincere worship for Allah alone, Creator of all; the obedient outrank deniers
sections.meaning: The Qur’an comes from Allah, so worship Him with a religion kept pure for Him. The idolators say their gods only bring them nearer to Allah; that is a lie. He has no son. He made the heavens, the night and day, and you from one soul. Disbelief costs Him nothing; gratitude pleases Him.
points: The Book is from Allah: so worship Him, sincere in religion
Idolators worship others “to bring us nearer”; Allah will judge that lie
Had He wanted a son, He would choose; He is the One, the Subduer
Night wrapped over day, sun and moon, you from one soul
He needs nothing; He hates disbelief; man prays in hardship, then forgets
Is the night-worshipper equal to them? Do the knowing equal the ignorant?
sections.matters: It sets the surah’s one demand in its first two ayat: al-dīn al-khāliṣ, worship kept pure for Allah. Everything after is proof for it or a warning against breaking it, and the idolators’ excuse in ayah 3 is the target.
sections.story: The Makkan idolators admitted Allah created everything, yet worshipped idols shaped like angels, hoping the angels would intercede for them. Ayah 8 is reportedly about ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah or Abū Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Mughīrah; ayah 9 reportedly about Abū Bakr, or ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, or others.
explained: The Qur’an is sent down in truth by al-ʿAzīz al-Ḥakīm, so worship Allah mukhliṣan lahu al-dīn: no partner, no show. Allah accepts no deed unless it is purely His. The idolators dressed shirk up as seeking nearness (zulfā) through intercessors, comparing Allah to a king who needs courtiers. He needs no one, and He takes no son.

Look at the proof: He wraps night over day, runs the sun and moon to a set term, and shaped you in three darknesses from one soul. Your faith adds nothing to Him and your denial costs Him nothing, but He loves gratitude. Man begs Him in trouble and forgets Him in ease. The night-worshipper is not his equal.
teaches: Ikhlāṣ is the whole religion: a deed with a partner in it is not accepted.
“They bring us nearer to Allah” is the oldest excuse for shirk.
Allah does not need your worship; He wants it for your good.
Fear and hope belong together, especially in the night prayer.
Real knowledge shows in how you worship, not in what you claim.
sections.hook: Mukhliṣan lahu al-dīn closes ayah 2, then 11 and 14. Ayah 6 ends with a question (fa-annā tuṣrafūn); ayah 9 asks another (hal yastawī). The ۞ sits at ayah 8, page 459.

sections.title: Fear Allah, emigrate if needed; the losers burn, the God-fearing get chambers
sections.meaning: Believers are told to fear Allah, and if a land blocks their worship, His earth is wide; the patient are paid without limit. The Prophet ﷺ declares he worships Allah alone and fears disobeying Him. The losers lose themselves and their families under layers of fire; those who shun ṭāghūt and listen well get chambers.
points: Fear your Lord; Allah’s earth is wide; the patient are paid without count
I am commanded to worship Him sincerely and be the first Muslim
I fear disobeying Him; worship what you like; the losers lose family
Canopies of fire above and below; O My servants, fear Me
Good news for those who shun ṭāghūt and follow the best of speech
You can’t save one doomed to Fire; the fearful get chambers on chambers
Rain becomes springs, then crops, then yellow, then debris: a reminder
sections.matters: This is the surah’s message to believers under pressure: patience is rewarded without measure, and moving to save your religion is allowed. The Prophet ﷺ models the sincerity demanded in section 1, and the two endings, fire in layers or chambers in layers, are set side by side.
sections.story: Ayah 10 is reportedly about Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib and the emigrants to Abyssinia. Ayah 13 came when the Prophet ﷺ was invited to his fathers’ religion. Ayat 17–18 reportedly concern Zayd ibn ʿAmr, Abū Dharr and Salmān, who shunned idols before Islam, or the converts who followed Abū Bakr.
explained: Allah addresses the believers with love, “O My servants,” and commands taqwā. Doing good brings good here and in the Hereafter, and if a place stops you worshipping, His earth is wide: leave. The patient are paid without measure, poured out, not weighed. The Prophet ﷺ then states his own stand: sincere worship, first to submit, afraid to disobey.

Worship what you like, but the losers lose themselves and their families, under fire above and below; Allah says this to frighten His servants into taqwā. The other side: those who shun ṭāghūt, turn to Allah and follow the best of what they hear get chambers built over chambers. Ayah 21 ends with rain that becomes debris, like this world.
teaches: If your surroundings stop your religion, move; Allah’s earth is wide.
Patience is the one deed paid without a scale.
The caller must be the first to do what he calls to.
Listen to everything, follow only the best of it.
This world is green, then yellow, then dust: don’t build on it.
sections.hook: “O My servants” opens ayah 10 and closes ayah 16. Qul opens 10, 11, 13 and 14. Ulū al-albāb ends 18 and 21. Ghuraf in 20 gives the surah its other name, al-Ghuraf.

sections.title: Open hearts soften to the Qur’an; one master beats many; everyone dies
sections.meaning: Whose heart Allah opened walks in light; hard hearts are lost. The Qur’an, the best speech, consistent and repeated, makes the God-fearing shiver, then soften. Earlier deniers were disgraced. Parable: a slave of quarrelling owners against a slave of one master. You will die, they will die, then dispute before Allah.
points: A heart opened to Islam walks in light; hardened hearts are astray
The best speech: consistent, repeated; skins shiver, then soften
Facing the Fire with his face; earlier deniers tasted disgrace
Every kind of example, in a clear Arabic Qur’an, without crookedness
A slave of quarrelling partners vs. a slave of one man: not equal
You will die, they will die, then you dispute before your Lord
sections.matters: It shows what the sincere religion does inside a person: an opened chest, skin that shivers and then softens. The slave parable is the surah’s clearest picture of shirk against tawḥīd. Ayah 30 was recited by Abū Bakr when the Prophet ﷺ died.
sections.story: Ayah 23 reportedly came when the companions asked the Prophet ﷺ, “Tell us something,” and some count it Madinan. Ayah 30 reportedly answered those waiting for his death. When ayah 31 came, az-Zubayr asked whether their worldly disputes would be repeated; he was told yes, until every right is paid.
explained: Sharḥ al-ṣadr: Allah widens a chest to accept Islam, and that person walks on light. Its sign is turning to the eternal home and preparing for death. Hard hearts don’t soften when Allah is mentioned. His speech is aḥsan al-ḥadīth: its parts confirm each other, repeating promise and warning until skins shiver, then skins and hearts relax in His remembrance.

The denier meets the worst punishment with his face, hands tied, like nations before, struck from where they never expected. The Qur’an gives every kind of parable in plain Arabic. One: a slave pulled apart by quarrelling owners against a slave of one man: the idolator against the sincere believer. All of you will die, then argue before your Lord.
teaches: Ask Allah to open your chest; the sign is preparing for death.
Let the Qur’an move you: fear at its warnings, calm at its mercy.
Shirk tears a person apart; tawḥīd gives one master and rest.
Even the Prophet ﷺ dies; only what you did survives.
Settle your disputes here; they will be replayed there.
sections.hook: Ayat 22 and 24 both open with a-fa-man, like 19 before them. Ayah 23 pairs opposites: taqshaʿirru then talīnu, yahdī then yuḍlil. Ayah 30: four words, the surah’s shortest. The section fills page 461 exactly.

sections.title: Liars face Hell, believers win; Allah is enough against their powerless idols
sections.meaning: Juz 24 opens with the worst wrong: lying about Allah and denying the truth. Those who bring and believe the truth get all they wish. They threatened the Prophet ﷺ with their idols, so Allah asks: is He not enough for His servant? Their idols can neither remove His harm nor hold back His mercy.
points: Who is more unjust than one who lies about Allah and denies truth?
Truth-bringer and believers: the God-fearing get all they wish, sins removed
Is Allah not enough for His servant? They scare you with idols
They admit Allah created all; can idols undo His harm? Ḥasbiya Allāh
Work your way, I work mine; you will see who is disgraced
The Book is for people; guidance or straying is their own; you’re no manager
sections.matters: Here the fight becomes personal: Quraysh threatened the Prophet ﷺ with the anger of their gods. The answer, ḥasbiya Allāh, is the surah’s motto for anyone pressured to sin. The section also fixes the Prophet’s job: deliver the Book, not force hearts.
sections.story: The idolators told the Prophet ﷺ: stop insulting our gods or they will strike you with madness. Ayah 36 answered them. When he asked whether their idols could remove Allah’s harm, they reportedly fell silent, or said “they cannot, but they intercede,” and “Sufficient for me is Allah” came down.
explained: No one is more unjust than one who invents lies about Allah, giving Him partners or a son, then rejects the truth when it reaches him. Hell is his home. Opposite: the one who brought the truth, the Prophet ﷺ, and those who believed it: the muttaqūn. Whatever they wish is theirs, their worst deeds erased, their best rewarded.

Is Allah not kāfin, enough, for His servant? Yet they scare the Prophet ﷺ with idols. Ask them who made the heavens and earth; they say Allah. Can those idols lift a harm Allah wants, or hold back His mercy? No. Ḥasbiya Allāh. Let them work their way; punishment will show who was right. His job is only to deliver.
teaches: Lying about Allah and rejecting His truth is the worst injustice.
Ḥasbiya Allāh: say it when anyone threatens you for obeying Him.
Whatever cannot harm or help you does not deserve your fear.
You are responsible to deliver the truth, not to force it.
sections.hook: Juz 24 starts here at ayah 32 (the ۞ on page 462). Two “Is not Allah…?” questions, 36 and 37, mirror each other: no guide for the misled, no misleader for the guided.

sections.title: Allah takes souls, owns intercession, judges disputes; man forgets Him in ease
sections.meaning: Allah takes souls at death and in sleep, keeping some, returning others: a sign. Their idols own nothing and cannot think; all intercession is Allah’s. Hearts shrink when Allah alone is named and rejoice at idols. No ransom is accepted that Day. Man calls Allah in trouble, then credits his knowledge; provision is a test.
points: Souls taken at death and in sleep; some kept, others released
Idols own nothing, don’t reason; intercession belongs entirely to Allah
Hearts shrink at “Allah alone,” rejoice when idols are named
The duʿāʾ: Creator, Knower of unseen, You will judge between servants
The whole earth twice over would not ransom them; the mocked punishment surrounds them
Man prays in harm, then says “my knowledge”; it is a test
sections.matters: Sleep is a nightly rehearsal of death and waking, so the resurrection they deny is something they live through daily. It also kills the intercession excuse from ayah 3: intercession is Allah’s alone. Ayah 46 gives the duʿāʾ the Prophet ﷺ opened his night prayer with.
sections.story: No specific incident for most of it. Ayah 49 is reportedly about Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Mughīrah, and ayah 50 recalls Qārūn, who said the same words. Ayah 51 is a threat to Quraysh, who reportedly then suffered seven years of drought before relief.
explained: Allah yatawaffā al-anfus: He takes souls fully at death, and takes them in sleep too. Those decreed to die He keeps; the rest He sends back until their term. Whoever does this every night can raise the dead. So why take idols as intercessors? They own nothing and cannot think. All intercession is Allah’s, by His permission alone.

Their hearts recoil at “Allah alone” and rejoice at idols. The Prophet ﷺ leaves judgement to the Creator, Knower of all. That Day they would give the earth twice over as ransom, and what they mocked surrounds them. Man begs Allah in harm, then says “I earned this by knowledge.” No: wealth is a trial for good and bad alike.
teaches: Every night you die a little; every morning is a small resurrection.
Ask intercession only from the One who owns it.
Test your heart: does “Allah alone” make it shrink or shine?
Wealth after hardship is a trial, not a certificate of merit.
Recite ayah 46 when disputes confuse you; leave judgement to Allah.
sections.hook: Ayah 49 repeats ayah 8 almost word for word (harm → prayer → favour → forgetting). Ayah 45 sets two “when”s against each other. Ayah 46 opens with the surah’s only Allāhumma.

sections.title: Don’t despair of Allah’s mercy; return before punishment, or regret it forever
sections.meaning: The surah’s most hopeful call: O My servants who went too far, do not despair; Allah forgives all sins for whoever returns. Turn back, submit and follow the Qur’an before punishment comes suddenly, or a soul will cry “my regret” and beg for another chance. Liars’ faces blackened; the God-fearing saved. Allah holds every key.
points: O My servants who sinned: don’t despair; Allah forgives all sins
Return, submit, follow the best revelation before sudden punishment
Three regrets: “I neglected,” “had Allah guided me,” “another chance”
Yes! My signs came, but you denied them and were arrogant
Liars’ faces blackened; the God-fearing saved, untouched by harm
Creator of all, Disposer of all, Owner of every key; deniers lose
sections.matters: Ayah 53 is called the ayah of greatest relief in the Qur’an. It throws the door open to every sinner, even those who killed and committed zinā, but 54–59 set the deadline: repentance works before death, not after, when regret is useless.
sections.story: Idolators who had killed and committed zinā asked the Prophet ﷺ if there was expiation for them; ayah 53 came down. Others say it was for Waḥshī, who feared his Islam would be rejected, or for tortured Muslims like ʿAyyāsh who had recanted; ʿUmar wrote it out and sent it.
explained: Asrafū ʿalā anfusihim: they went too far against themselves. Still Allah calls them “My servants” and forbids despair, because He forgives all sins, even shirk, for whoever repents. The way in: anībū, return with the heart; aslimū, submit with the limbs; follow the best that was revealed. Do it before the punishment arrives, suddenly, while you are not looking.

Otherwise a soul will cry yā ḥasratā, “my regret,” over neglecting Allah’s right, or plead “had Allah guided me,” or, seeing the punishment, beg for one more turn. The reply: My signs came, and you denied them out of pride. That Day the liars’ faces are black; the God-fearing are led to safety. Allah, Creator of everything, holds every key.
teaches: No sin is too big for repentance; despair itself is the danger.
Repentance has a deadline: before death, before the punishment lands.
“If only Allah had guided me” is not an excuse; His signs came.
Never tell anyone Allah will not forgive them.
The keys are in His hand, so ask Him, not the doorkeepers.
sections.hook: The section starts at the ۞ on page 464 with the surah’s third “O My servants” (after 10 and 16). Three regrets follow in 56–58, all answered by one “Yes!” (balā) in 59.

sections.title: Shirk wipes out deeds; they underrate Allah; the Trumpet, then perfect judgement
sections.meaning: Told to worship idols, the Prophet ﷺ answers: you ignorant people! Every prophet was warned that shirk cancels all deeds. They never valued Allah rightly: the earth is His handful, the heavens folded in His right hand. The Trumpet kills all, then raises all; the earth shines, the record opens, every soul paid in full.
points: Do you order me to worship other than Allah, you ignorant ones?
If you associate, your work is worthless; so worship Allah, be grateful
They underrate Allah; earth in His grip, heavens folded in His right hand
Trumpet: all fall dead except whom He wills; blown again, all stand
Earth shines, record placed, prophets and witnesses brought; full justice
sections.matters: The surah returns to its opening command, worship Allah alone, and states the cost of breaking it: shirk wipes out a lifetime of deeds, even a prophet’s. Then it shows why: the One they belittle will hold the earth in His hand while every soul is judged.
sections.story: Quraysh invited the Prophet ﷺ to worship their gods, offering to worship his God alongside him; ayah 64 answered them. Ayah 67 reportedly concerns Quraysh. A rabbi once described Allah holding the heavens and earths on His fingers, and the Prophet ﷺ smiled in agreement and recited ayah 67.
explained: The idolators wanted a deal: worship our gods and we will worship yours. The sharp answer: is it other than Allah you tell me to worship, you ignorant ones? Every prophet before was told the same rule: la-in ashrakta la-yaḥbaṭanna ʿamaluk, associate anything with Allah and your work collapses. So worship Allah alone and be grateful, above all for guidance.

Mā qadarū Allāha ḥaqqa qadrih: they never grasped His greatness, or they would not give Him partners. On the Day the earth is His handful, the heavens rolled in His right hand. The Trumpet is blown: all fall dead except whom Allah wills; blown again, they stand staring. The earth shines, the record opens, witnesses come; no one is wronged.
teaches: No deal with shirk, whatever is offered in return.
One act of shirk can erase a lifetime of good deeds.
Belittling Allah is the root of every deviation.
Be grateful for guidance itself; it is the greatest blessing.
The judgement is in full light, with witnesses; no one is wronged.
sections.hook: Bali Allāha fa-ʿbud (66) echoes the surah’s first command, fa-ʿbudi Allāha (2). Ayah 68 has two blasts: nufikha… thumma nufikha fīhi ukhrā. Ayah 69 lists four events: shone, placed, brought, judged.

sections.title: Zumar: deniers driven to Hell, the God-fearing welcomed to Paradise with praise
sections.meaning: Disbelievers are driven to Hell in groups. Its gates open; its keepers ask: did messengers not warn you of this Day? Yes, they admit; punishment is due. The God-fearing are led to Paradise in groups, gates open, greeted with peace. They praise Allah who kept His promise; angels around the Throne praise Him too.
points: Driven to Hell in groups; keepers ask: didn’t messengers warn you?
Enter Hell’s gates forever; wretched home of the arrogant
Led to Paradise in groups; gates open; “Peace, you did well, enter”
They praise Allah who kept His promise; settle anywhere in Paradise
Angels around the Throne glorify Him; praise to the Lord of the worlds
sections.matters: The surah’s name comes from here: two processions in groups (zumar), one to each gate. Every warning and promise in the surah lands in these five ayat, and the whole thing ends where creation began, with al-ḥamdu lillāh.
sections.story: No specific incident. It describes the end of the two groups the surah has contrasted throughout. The Prophet ﷺ said he would be the first to knock on Paradise’s gate, and that its first group would enter with faces like the full moon.
explained: Sīqa: the disbelievers are driven, pushed and thirsty, to Hell in groups. On arrival its gates open, so the heat hits them at once. The keepers scold them: did messengers from among you not warn you of this meeting? Yes, they say, but the word of punishment came true. Enter its gates forever, a wretched home for the arrogant.

The God-fearing are led gently to Paradise in groups, each with its like, the best first. Its gates stand open before they arrive, and the keepers greet them: salāmun ʿalaykum, ṭibtum, you have become pure, enter forever. They answer: praise to Allah who kept His promise and gave us this land to settle wherever we wish.
The angels circle the Throne praising Him, judgement is done in truth, and, from no named speaker, it is said: praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds. All creation joins in.
teaches: You will walk in with your kind; choose your group now.
“Didn’t messengers warn you?” The warning you heard will be quoted back.
Arrogance is what keeps people out of Paradise.
Paradise is Allah’s promise kept; praise Him for it.
Everything begins and ends with al-ḥamdu lillāh.
sections.hook: 71 and 73 are twins: wa-sīqa alladhīna… zumaran… ḥattā idhā jāʾūhā… wa-qāla lahum khazanatuhā. The one-letter difference: futiḥat (71) becomes wa-futiḥat (73). Ḥamd appears three times in 74–75. Ayah 75 opens page 467.

groups.text: The Book comes from Allah, Mighty and Wise, sent in truth; so worship Him with your religion kept pure for Him.
Pure religion is Allah’s alone. Idolators claim their gods bring them nearer; He will judge that. He has no son: the One, the Subduer.
He wraps night over day, runs sun and moon to a term, made you from one soul in three darknesses. How are you turned away?
Allah needs no one, dislikes disbelief, loves gratitude. Man prays to Him in harm, then forgets Him in ease and sets up rivals.
Is the one praying through the night, fearing and hoping, like that? Those who know and those who don’t are not equal.
O believers, fear your Lord. Good for the good-doers; Allah’s earth is wide; the patient are paid without limit.
I am commanded to worship Allah sincerely and to be the first of the Muslims.
I fear the great Day if I disobey. I worship Allah alone; worship what you like. The losers lose themselves and their families.
Canopies of fire above them and below them. Allah frightens His servants with this: O My servants, fear Me.
Good news for those who shun ṭāghūt and turn to Allah, who listen to speech and follow the best of it: people of understanding.
You cannot save one doomed to the Fire. The God-fearing get chambers above chambers, rivers beneath; Allah never breaks His promise.
Rain sinks into springs, grows crops of many colours, then they yellow and crumble. A reminder for people of understanding.
A chest opened to Islam walks in light; hard hearts are lost. The best speech makes the fearful shiver, then softens their skins and hearts.
The wrongdoer meets the worst punishment with his face. Earlier deniers were hit from where they never expected; the Hereafter is worse.
Every kind of example in this Qur’an, clear Arabic without crookedness, so they may remember and be God-fearing.
A slave torn between quarrelling owners against a slave of one master: are they equal? Praise to Allah, but most don’t know.
You will die and they will die. Then on the Day of Resurrection you will dispute before your Lord.
Who is more unjust than one who lies about Allah and denies the truth when it comes? Hell is the disbelievers’ home.
The one who brought the truth and those who believed it are the God-fearing: all they wish, worst deeds erased, best deeds rewarded.
Is Allah not enough for His servant? They scare you with idols. Whom He misleads none guides; whom He guides none misleads.
They admit Allah created the heavens and earth. Can their idols undo His harm or hold back His mercy? Allah is sufficient for me.
Work your way; I work mine. You will learn who gets the disgracing punishment and the lasting one.
The Book is sent for people in truth. Guidance helps only oneself, straying harms only oneself; you are not their manager.
Allah takes souls at death and in sleep, keeps those decreed to die, releases the rest to their term: signs for thinkers.
Their intercessors own nothing and cannot think. All intercession is Allah’s; His is the dominion; to Him you return.
Hearts shrink when Allah alone is named and rejoice at idols. Say: O Allah, Creator, Knower of all, You will judge between Your servants.
The earth twice over would not ransom them. What they never reckoned appears, their evils appear, and the mocked punishment surrounds them.
Man prays in harm, then says “I earned this by knowledge.” A trial; earlier nations said it and fell. Allah widens and narrows provision.
O My servants who went too far against themselves: do not despair. Allah forgives all sins; He is Forgiving, Merciful.
Return to your Lord, submit, and follow the best revelation, before punishment comes suddenly and no one helps you.
Three regrets on that Day: my regret over neglecting Allah; had He guided me; if only I could go back and do good.
Yes! My signs came to you, but you denied them, were arrogant, and disbelieved.
Those who lied about Allah: faces blackened, Hell for the arrogant. Allah saves the God-fearing; no harm, no grief.
Allah is Creator and Disposer of all; His are the keys of the heavens and earth. Deniers of His signs are the losers.
Say: do you order me to worship other than Allah, you ignorant ones?
Revealed to you and every prophet before: associate partners and your work is void. So worship Allah and be among the grateful.
They never valued Allah rightly: the earth is His grip on the Day, the heavens folded in His right hand. Exalted above their shirk.
The Trumpet is blown: all in the heavens and earth fall dead except whom He wills. Blown again: they stand, looking on.
The earth shines with its Lord’s light, the record is placed, prophets and witnesses brought; judged in truth, every soul paid in full.
Deniers driven to Hell in groups; gates opened; keepers: didn’t messengers warn you? Yes. Enter forever, wretched home of the arrogant.
The God-fearing led to Paradise in groups, gates open: peace, you did well, enter forever. Praise to Allah who kept His promise.
Angels ring the Throne glorifying their Lord. Judgement is done in truth, and it is said: praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

1.explain: Tanzīl al-kitāb: the Qur’an is sent down from Allah Himself, al-ʿAzīz (Mighty, never overcome) and al-Ḥakīm (Wise in all He says, does and decrees). A Book from such a Sender has no doubt in it.

2.explain: Sent down bil-ḥaqq, in truth, so the response is: worship Allah mukhliṣan lahu al-dīn, keeping the whole religion pure for Him, with no partner and no show. Dīn here means worship and obedience.

3.explain: Al-dīn al-khāliṣ: only pure worship is Allah’s, and He accepts nothing mixed. The idolators’ excuse: “they bring us nearer (zulfā),” treating Allah like a king who needs courtiers. He will judge that dispute. A stubborn liar is not guided.

4.explain: Law arāda: a supposition of the impossible. Had Allah wanted a son He would have chosen from His own creation, not what they claim (angels, ʿUzayr, ʿĪsā). Subḥānah: far above that. Al-Wāḥid al-Qahhār: One, and everything is subdued to Him.

5.explain: Yukawwir: He wraps night over day and day over night, each chasing the other, like winding a turban. Sun and moon run to a fixed term, the Day of Resurrection. Al-ʿAzīz al-Ghaffār: Mighty, yet forgiving to whoever turns back.

6.explain: One soul, Ādam; from him Ḥawwāʾ. Eight pairs of livestock: sheep, goats, camels, cattle. You are shaped stage after stage, nuṭfah to ʿalaqah to muḍghah, in three darknesses: belly, womb, placenta. That is your Lord, so where are you turning?

7.explain: Allah is Ghanī: your disbelief costs Him nothing, your faith adds nothing. Still He does not approve disbelief for His servants, and He is pleased with gratitude. No soul carries another’s burden; He knows what is in the chests.

8.explain: Ḍurr: illness, poverty, danger at sea. Then man calls on Allah alone, munīban, turning back to Him. Given relief, he forgets and sets up andād, rivals, leading others astray too. “Enjoy your disbelief a little” is a threat.
8.why: Reportedly revealed about ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah, or about Abū Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Mughīrah; others say it is general, about every disbeliever.

9.explain: Qānit: devoutly obedient, praying ānāʾ al-layl, through the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for mercy. Is he like the man of ayah 8? Only ulū al-albāb, people of understanding, see the difference.
9.why: Reportedly about Abū Bakr; or Abū Bakr and ʿUmar; or ʿUthmān; or Ibn Masʿūd, ʿAmmār and Salmān. One report names ʿAmmār as “those who know” and Abū Ḥudhayfah al-Makhzūmī as “those who do not.”

10.explain: Yā ʿibād: Allah addresses believers as His servants and commands taqwā. Good here and in the Hereafter. Arḍ Allāh wāsiʿah: if a land stops your worship, emigrate. The patient are paid bi-ghayri ḥisāb, poured out without measure.
10.why: Reportedly revealed about the emigrants to Abyssinia: Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib and his companions, who kept their religion under persecution, were patient, and emigrated.

11.explain: The Prophet ﷺ states his own orders: worship Allah mukhliṣan lahu al-dīn, the same words as ayah 2, with no shirk. The caller lives what he calls to.

12.explain: Awwal al-muslimīn: first of this ummah to submit. Since he calls people to their Lord, he must be first to obey his own call: submission in outward deeds, sincerity in the inward ones.

13.explain: Even the Messenger ﷺ says: if I disobeyed my Lord, I would fear the punishment of a tremendous Day. A conditional: if it applies to him, it applies far more to everyone else.
13.why: Reportedly said when he was invited to the religion of his forefathers.

14.explain: Allāha aʿbud: “Allah I worship,” my religion kept pure for Him. It is the third mukhliṣan lahu in the surah (ayat 2, 11, 14), the Prophet ﷺ repeating his stand before the challenge that follows.

15.explain: “Worship what you like besides Him” is a threat and a disowning, like “do what you will.” The real losers lose themselves to the Fire and lose their families: separated forever, or their prepared place in Paradise given to others.

16.explain: Ẓulal: layers or canopies of fire above them, and below them more layers, like a bed with coverings. Allah describes this to frighten His servants away from sin: yā ʿibād fa-ttaqūn, “O My servants, fear Me.”

17.explain: Ṭāghūt: idols, or any worship of other than Allah. Those who avoid it and anābū, turn back to Allah, get bushrā, good news, in this life, at death, in the grave and on the Day.
17.why: Reportedly revealed about Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl, Abū Dharr and Salmān, who rejected idols before Islam; or about ʿUthmān, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, Saʿd, Saʿīd, Ṭalḥah and az-Zubayr, who asked Abū Bakr about his faith and believed.

18.explain: Al-qawl: the Qur’an, or all speech. They listen, then follow aḥsanah, the best: the Qur’an over everything else, the firmer option over the concession, pardon over revenge. That discernment is why they are ulū al-albāb.
18.why: Reportedly about the same men as ayah 17: Abū Dharr and Salmān heard every religion before choosing Islam, and the early converts believed after hearing Abū Bakr.

19.explain: Kalimat al-ʿadhāb: the decree “I will fill Hell,” settled on those who persist in denial. A-fa-anta tunqidh: can you, Muḥammad ﷺ, rescue someone already in the Fire? You cannot force guidance.
19.why: The Prophet ﷺ longed for the faith of people whose misery was already decreed; this came down. Reportedly it concerns Abū Lahab, his children and relatives who held back from faith.

20.explain: Ghuraf: chambers built storey above storey, so fine their inside shows from outside, seen from below like bright stars on the horizon, rivers running beneath. Waʿd Allāh: promised, and Allah never breaks a promise.

21.explain: Rain sinks into the earth and comes out as yanābīʿ, springs, stored for use. It grows crops of changing colours, which yellow, dry and crumble into ḥuṭām. That is this world: green, then old, then gone.

22.explain: Sharaḥa ṣadrah: Allah widens a chest so it accepts Islam and walks on light. Its sign: longing for the eternal home, pulling away from this deceptive one, preparing for death. Hard hearts, unmoved by Allah’s mention, are clearly lost.

23.explain: Aḥsan al-ḥadīth, the best speech. Mutashābih: its parts match and confirm each other. Mathānī: promise and warning, stories and rulings, repeated. Warnings make the fearful’s skin shiver; mercy softens skin and heart. No swooning, just tears and awe.
23.why: Reportedly the companions said, “If only you would tell us something (ḥaddithnā),” or grew weary and asked for it, and this came down. Some count it among the surah’s two Madinan ayat.

24.explain: Yattaqī bi-wajhih: thrown into the Fire with hands chained to his neck, he can shield himself only with his face, the noblest part. Is he like one who arrives safe? The keepers say: “Taste what you earned.”

25.explain: The nations before them called their messengers liars, and the punishment came min ḥaythu lā yashʿurūn: from a direction they never imagined, while they felt safe and heedless, at dawn or at midday rest.

26.explain: Khizy: disgrace in this life, by destruction, transformation or killing, exposed before Allah and people. Yet the punishment of the Hereafter is greater. So let today’s deniers beware of the same.

27.explain: Mathal: every kind of example, of the good and the wicked, of tawḥīd and shirk. Parables bring truths close to the mind, so that people remember and act.

28.explain: Qur’ānan ʿarabiyyan: plain Arabic, clear words, easy meanings. Ghayra dhī ʿiwaj: no crookedness, no contradiction, no confusion, in wording or meaning. Its aim: that they gain taqwā and avoid disbelief.

29.explain: A slave owned by mutashākisūn, quarrelling partners who each demand service at once, against a slave salaman, wholly one man’s, who knows what his master wants and is at rest. The idolator and the believer. Not equal.

30.explain: Mayyit, with the doubled yāʾ: one who will die, not one already dead. You will die and they will die, so no gloating over anyone’s death. Abū Bakr recited this when the Prophet ﷺ died.
30.why: Reportedly revealed when the disbelievers were impatiently waiting for the Prophet’s ﷺ death.

31.explain: Takhtaṣimūn: you will dispute before your Lord. Believer against disbeliever, the wronged against the wrongdoer, truthful against liar. Every wrong between people is replayed and settled: good deeds handed over, or the victim’s sins loaded on.
31.why: When it came down, az-Zubayr asked, “Will our disputes in this world be repeated for us?” He was told yes, until everyone gets his right. Some companions did not understand it until they fought one another.

32.explain: Two falsehoods in one man: kadhaba ʿalā Allāh, lying about Him (partners, a son, false claims in His name), and kadhdhaba bil-ṣidq, rejecting the truth, the Qur’an, when it reached him. Hell is his home.

33.explain: Alladhī jāʾa bil-ṣidq: the one who brought the truth, the Prophet ﷺ (or Jibrīl, or every prophet). Ṣaddaqa bih: those who believed it, the Muslims (or Abū Bakr). Bringing truth and believing it: that is taqwā.

34.explain: Whatever they wish is theirs with their Lord, in Paradise: what no eye saw, no ear heard. Muḥsinīn: those who worship Allah as if seeing Him, and do good to His servants.

35.explain: Yukaffir: Allah wipes away aswaʾ, the worst they did, their sins, and pays them for aḥsan, the best they did, their good deeds. Sins covered, good rewarded in full.

36.explain: Kāfin ʿabdah: enough for His servant, the Prophet ﷺ, or, in another reading, His servants, the prophets. Yet they frighten him with idols that cannot hurt. Whoever Allah lets stray, no one guides.
36.why: The disbelievers threatened the Prophet ﷺ with the anger of their idols: “Stop insulting our gods, or they will strike you with madness.”

37.explain: The mirror of 36: whoever Allah guides, no one can mislead. ʿAzīz: unbeatable, so He protects His servant. Dhū intiqām: He takes retribution from His enemies, so beware what earns it.

38.explain: They admit Allah created the heavens and earth. Then: if Allah wants harm for me, can your idols remove it? If He wants mercy, can they hold it back? No. Ḥasbiya Allāh: Allah is enough for me.
38.why: Reportedly the Prophet ﷺ put this question to them and they fell silent; or they said, “They cannot undo what Allah decrees, but they intercede.” Then “Say: Allah is sufficient for me” came down.

39.explain: Iʿmalū ʿalā makānatikum: “work in your position,” your way, worshipping what has no power. Innī ʿāmil: I am working my way, sincere worship of Allah alone. A threat: soon you will know who was right.

40.explain: Two punishments: ʿadhāb yukhzīh, a disgracing one in this world (reportedly at Badr), and ʿadhāb muqīm, a lasting one in the Hereafter that never lifts. They knew who deserved it; stubbornness stopped them believing.

41.explain: The Book is sent lil-nās, for all people, in truth. Guidance profits only the guided; straying harms only the strayer. Wakīl: you are not their keeper, made to force belief on them. Deliver; the account is Allah’s.

42.explain: Yatawaffā: Allah takes souls fully at death, the greater death, and takes them in sleep, the lesser one. Those decreed to die He keeps; the rest return until their term. Every morning is a small resurrection: a sign for thinkers.

43.explain: Am ittakhadhū: or have they taken shufaʿāʾ, intercessors, besides Allah? Their idols own nothing, not an atom’s weight, and cannot even think: stone, wood, images, the dead. Who is more foolish than one who trusts them?

44.explain: Lillāhi al-shafāʿatu jamīʿan: all intercession belongs to Allah. No one intercedes except by His permission, for whom He is pleased with. He owns the heavens and earth, so ask Him, and to Him you return for judgement.

45.explain: Ishmaʾazzat: their hearts shrink, recoil, puff up in pride when Allah alone is mentioned with no partner. Name their idols, and they yastabshirūn, light up with joy. It shows what the heart really wants.

46.explain: Allāhumma fāṭir al-samāwāt: O Allah, Originator of the heavens and earth, Knower of the hidden and the seen. You will judge Your servants’ disputes. The Prophet ﷺ opened his night prayer with these words, adding “guide me to the truth.”

47.explain: If the wrongdoers owned the whole earth and as much again, they would offer it all as ransom from sūʾ al-ʿadhāb, the worst punishment. Refused. And what they never reckoned appears: deeds they thought good, counted against them.

48.explain: Badā lahum: the evils they earned, shirk and wronging Allah’s friends, come into view as punishment. Ḥāqa bihim: the torment they used to laugh at closes around them.

49.explain: Ayah 8 again. In harm, man calls Us; given a favour, he says innamā ūtītuhu ʿalā ʿilm: “I got this by my know-how,” or “because Allah knows I deserve it.” No: it is fitnah, a test of gratitude.
49.why: Reportedly revealed about Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Mughīrah.

50.explain: Qad qālahā: the same boast was said before them, by Qārūn, “I was given it because of my knowledge,” and by his kind. Their earnings did not save them when the punishment came.

51.explain: Sayyiʾāt here means the punishments their deeds earned. Those before were struck, and the wrongdoers among these, Quraysh, will be struck too. Muʿjizīn: they cannot escape or outrun Allah. Reportedly they then suffered seven years of drought before relief.

52.explain: Yabsuṭu wa-yaqdir: Allah widens provision for some and tightens it for others, righteous or wicked alike. So wealth proves no merit; sometimes He restricts it out of kindness, since plenty would make people transgress.

53.explain: Asrafū ʿalā anfusihim: went too far against themselves, yet still “My servants.” Lā taqnaṭū: never despair. Allah forgives all sins, even shirk, murder and zinā, for whoever repents. Whoever makes people despair after this rejects Allah’s Book.
53.why: Reported causes: idolators who had killed and committed zinā asked if repentance was open to them; Waḥshī doubted his Islam could be accepted; tortured Muslims who had recanted (ʿAyyāsh, Hishām, al-Walīd) thought themselves beyond forgiveness, so ʿUmar wrote it out and sent it to them.

54.explain: Anībū: return to your Lord with the heart. Aslimū: submit to Him with the limbs, sincerely. Do it before the punishment arrives, because then no one can help you. Repentance has a deadline.

55.explain: Aḥsan mā unzila: the best of what was sent down, the Qur’an, all of it good, the finest of all scriptures. Follow its commands, avoid what it forbids, before the punishment comes baghtatan, suddenly, unnoticed.

56.explain: The first regret. Yā ḥasratā: “O my grief!” over what I neglected fī janb Allāh, of Allah’s right and obedience. Worse, I was among the sākhirīn, mocking His religion, His Book and His people.

57.explain: The second regret, dressed as an excuse: “Had Allah guided me, I would have been God-fearing.” Law here is a wish, not a real condition; blaming destiny is a false plea that collapses on that Day.

58.explain: The third regret, on seeing the punishment: law anna lī karrah, “if only I had one more turn” to go back and do good. Impossible, and pointless: sent back, they would repeat what they did.

59.explain: Balā: “Yes indeed!” Allah answers the excuse of 57. My signs did reach you, the Qur’an itself, but you called them lies, were too proud to follow, and chose disbelief. Guidance was given; you refused it.

60.explain: Those who lied about Allah, giving Him partners or a son, will have faces muswaddah, blackened, known to everyone gathered. They blackened the face of truth with lies, so their faces are blackened. Hell for the arrogant.

61.explain: Yunajjī: Allah rescues the God-fearing bi-mafāzatihim, by their success, the deeds and the taqwā that carry them through. Another reading, mafāzātihim: by the paths that led to it. No harm touches them, no grief.

62.explain: Khāliqu kulli shayʾ: everything other than Allah is created; nothing is eternal beside Him. Wakīl: in charge of everything, with full knowledge, power and wisdom over what He manages.

63.explain: Maqālīd: keys, a word borrowed from Persian; or treasures. The keys of the heavens and earth, rain, plants, provision and mercy, are in His hand alone. Whoever denies His signs has lost everything worth having.

64.explain: A-fa-ghayra Allāh: “Is it other than Allah you order me to worship?” Ayyuhā al-jāhilūn: you ignorant ones, because only ignorance of who Allah is could suggest worshipping what cannot help or harm.
64.why: The idolators invited the Prophet ﷺ to worship their gods, offering to worship his God alongside him; or Quraysh called him back to the religion of his forefathers. This was the reply.

65.explain: Revealed to him and every prophet before: la-in ashrakta la-yaḥbaṭanna ʿamaluk, if you associate anything with Allah, all your work collapses. Addressed to the Prophet ﷺ, who was protected from shirk, but aimed at everyone else.

66.explain: Bali Allāha fa-ʿbud: no, worship Allah, Him alone. Be among the shākirīn, grateful for worldly blessings and even more for religious ones, guidance and sincerity above all. Gratitude also guards against self-admiration.

67.explain: Mā qadarū Allāha ḥaqqa qadrih: they never valued Allah as He deserves. On the Day the earth is His qabḍah, handful, and the heavens are rolled up in His right hand: believed as revealed, with no likeness to creation.
67.why: Reportedly revealed about Quraysh. A rabbi told the Prophet ﷺ that Allah will hold the heavens, earths, trees, water and all creation on His fingers and say “I am the King”; the Prophet ﷺ smiled in agreement and recited this ayah.

68.explain: Al-ṣūr: a great horn blown by Isrāfīl. Ṣaʿiqa: all in the heavens and earth fall dead or senseless, except whom Allah wills. After “forty” (days, months or years unknown) it is blown again, and all stand, staring.

69.explain: Ashraqat al-arḍ: the earth shines with its Lord’s light when He comes to judge. The record of deeds is opened. Prophets testify that they delivered; witnesses too: this ummah, the angels, even one’s own limbs. No one is wronged.

70.explain: Wuffiyat: every soul is paid in full for what it did, good and bad. He knows best what they do, so He needs no scribe and no witness. The whole creation will admit the verdict was just.

71.explain: Sīqa: driven harshly to Hell zumaran, in groups, each with its like. Its gates open on arrival. The keepers rebuke: didn’t messengers from among you warn you of this Day? Yes, they admit, but the word of punishment is due.

72.explain: Qīla: it is said, by no named speaker, so all creation agrees they deserve it. Enter Hell’s gates, forever, with no relief. Biʾsa mathwā: a wretched home for the mutakabbirīn, too proud to accept the truth.

73.explain: Sīqa again, but gently, with honour: to Paradise in groups, the best first, each with its like. Wa-futiḥat: the gates already open. Salāmun ʿalaykum ṭibtum: peace, you have become pure, so enter forever. Their entering is left unsaid.

74.explain: Their first words inside: al-ḥamdu lillāh, praise to Allah who kept His promise. Awrathanā al-arḍ: He gave us the land of Paradise to inherit, to settle wherever we wish and visit whom we wish. A fine reward for workers.

75.explain: Ḥāffīn: the angels ringing the Throne, glorifying with praise. Judgement is finished in truth, and al-ḥamdu lillāhi rabbi al-ʿālamīn is said by no named speaker: all creation praises His justice. Creation began with praise (6:1) and ends with it.
